title: Senior asks: DELETE ?action=delete&file=ghost.txt. The file does not exist. Which status does the client get?
explain: findFileActions() runs first. It checks the extension, and .txt is not supported, so it throws UnsupportedFormatException. The controller maps this to the default 400. Only ghost.csv or ghost.json would reach is_file() and give 404. The order of checks decides the answer.

title: Senior asks: index.php runs new FileService(...) on every request. Is that a performance problem?
options: Yes. Objects must be created once and kept in memory.
No. PHP starts fresh for each request. A few small objects cost almost nothing.
Yes. Each request loads the whole storage folder into memory.
No, because PHP keeps the objects between requests.
explain: With PHP-FPM or Apache, each request starts a clean script. Nothing stays in memory between requests. The constructor only stores a path and a list of strategies. It does not read storage/. So the cost is tiny. Real work (disk, parsing) is what you should watch.

title: Senior asks: the page sends the body {} to write for notes.json. What is in the file after that?
options: An error: Request body is not valid JSON.
explain: With assoc = true, an empty JSON object becomes an empty PHP array. decodeJson() accepts it (is_array is true). json_encode of an empty array is []. So {} turns into [] on disk. PHP arrays have no empty-object type. Use stdClass if you must keep {}.

pr.title: Shorter listFiles() with glob()
pr.author: olha-dev
pr.body: One line instead of seven. Same result.

explain: Not the same result. glob() returns full paths, not file names. It is case-sensitive, so A.CSV is missed (isSupported() lowercases). GLOB_BRACE does not exist on some systems, such as Alpine. The formats are hard-coded and ignore the strategy list. Keep the filter and use array_values() so JSON stays a list.

title: PHP 8. What does this print?
explain: empty() is true for "0" (the string zero is falsy in PHP). But "0.0" and " " are non-empty strings, so they are truthy. A form field with the value 0 counts as empty. Use $value === '' or isset() when 0 is valid.

title: An immutable value object. What does this print?
explain: A readonly property cannot change after it is set. So add() does not change $this. It builds a new Money with the new value. $a stays 100 and $b is 150. This is the "with" pattern for value objects: no side effects, safe to share.

title: Open /product/999 (no such id): a 500 error page, not 404. Tap the bug.
explain: find() returns null when the row does not exist. Then null->getName() throws an Error and the user sees a 500. Check for null and call createNotFoundException(). AI code often forgets this case.

title: Some inputs are empty, but hasEmpty() always returns false. Tap the bug.
explain: return true inside each() returns from the callback, not from hasEmpty(). In each(), true only means continue. So the last line always runs. Use a variable, and return false in the callback to stop the loop.
